newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian president hails Clinton victory.
newsitem.headline: Indian president hails Clinton victory.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma hailed U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election on Wednesday, and praised Clinton's first term as a landmark in bilateral relations.

"During your presidency, cooperation between India and the United States has greatly expanded. Trade and investment have increased several fold and we have embarked on new areas of cooperation," Sharma said in a letter to Clinton.
Indian officials said that, apart from formal official greetings to Clinton, Indian leaders could not be expected to say much on his re-election triumph.

"We have our problems with the U.S., much of which arose during the run-up to the (U.S.) election. The new administration will get more time to look into that," said Rasheed Talib, an independent political analyst.

State-run Doordarshan television reported Clinton's victory without comment. The news was the third main story, behind one on the framing of criminal cheating charges against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao on Wednesday.
During his first term Clinton pointedly declined to criticise India for alleged human rights abuses in Kashmir and for pursuing a nuclear weapons programme.
That did not deter Washington, however, from keeping the pressure on New Delhi on both fronts.

India, regarded as a threshold nuclear power, has refused to sign the Nuclear Non-proliferation Treaty or the recently introduced Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT), on both occasions against U.S. advice.
